item.title: Baker Mayfield and Buccaneers go from being at odds at start of camp to a monster contract to start season
item.description: Baker Mayfield's $165 million Buccaneers extension ties him with Joe Burrow and Josh Allen as the NFL's third-highest-paid quarterbacks overall.
item.content:encoded:
Baker Mayfield wasn't doing a new contract with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers once training camp began – until he did.

He was headed to free agency after this season – until he wasn't.

Funny how money has a way of changing things from one month to the next in the NFL.

PATRICK MAHOMES LEAPS PAST DAK PRESCOTT AS NFL'S HIGHEST-PAID QB WITH RECORD CHIEFS EXTENSION WORTH $504.75M

Mayfield has agreed to a three-year contract extension with the Bucs worth $165 million, OutKick has confirmed. The Bucs confirmed Mayfield isn't going anywhere.

The $55 million the quarterback will get on an annual average basis ties Mayfield with Joe Burrow, Josh Allen, Jordan Love, Trevor Lawrence and Matthew Stafford as the league's third-highest paid QBs.

Whether you think Mayfield should be in the same salary stratosphere as Burrow, Allen and last year's MVP is not the point.

The Bucs think so.

They moved much closer to Mayfield's negotiating position in the past week or so and that's the reason they've locked up the player who has thrown 95 TD passes in 51 starts for them.

A reminder: This wasn't initially headed in this direction.

The Bucs and their starting quarterback were at odds when training camp opened in July. The team had offered Mayfield a contract extension and he didn't believe it rewarded him to the extent he believed himself worth.

That led Mayfield to talk about a self-imposed training camp deadline for getting a new deal as being seemingly written in cement. It also led him to openly discuss betting on himself and the possibility of hitting free agency after the season.

There were wide-ranging pundit narratives that Mayfield plays better angry and we were about to see that this season.

That lasted a couple of days.

Mayfield's ire faded when the Bucs ignored the deadline and came back for more negotiations.

It outright disappeared when they offered him a deal that will keep him with the team and in a region he and his family like.

At a salary he obviously saw as more inviting than standing on negotiating deadlines and threats of 2027 free agency.

item.title: MAC files appeal to FBS committee to overturn Western Michigan-Michigan game, declare Broncos as winners
item.description: The MAC filed a formal NCAA appeal claiming the Western Michigan Broncos should be recognized as winners after a replay protocol error at Michigan.
item.content:encoded:
For a few minutes, the most stunning result of the early part of the college football season seemed to be the Western Michigan Broncos upsetting the heavily favored Michigan Wolverines at Michigan Stadium.

The Big House. Bryce Underwood, one of the most heavily promoted recruits of the past decade. New head coach Kyle Whittingham, known for his stability, consistency and avoiding major upsets while with the Utah Utes. And the Broncos took a 12-7 lead with just 38 seconds remaining and the Wolverines out of timeouts.

Everyone knows what happened next. Underwood's first Hail Mary attempt flew out of the back of the endzone, with the game clock on the broadcast and scoreboard showing 0:00. Game over. But after a poorly-explained review determined that there should have been an additional second added, Underwood was given a second opportunity. JJ Buchanan came down with it, and Wolverines fans stormed the field.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSIBLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Nearly everyone outside Michigan was perplexed, or downright angry, about the outcome. The Big Ten's explanation didn't make anything better either, with the conference saying the clocks were strobe-synced prior to the game, but that another clock viewed during the replay process had determined there was a second left. Even though the synced cameras showed zero seconds remaining.

Initially, it seemed like that would be the end of it. Western Michigan staff said they communicated with the Big Ten, reviewed the footage and were satisfied that proper procedure had been followed. Tuesday afternoon, though, that all changed.

The Mid-American Conference released a statement, announcing they'd filed a formal appeal to the NCAA FBS Oversight Committee and the College Football Playoff requesting that those two bodies recognize the Broncos as the true winners of the game.

"After further study and investigation, it is now evident that replay protocol was not properly followed in determining whether time remained on the game clock at the conclusion of the Western Michigan vs. Michigan football game," the statement says. "The established replay protocol requires that the game clock displayed on the program feed be used in determining whether time remained. Instead, the Big Ten Conference replay crew relied upon the clock feed embedded within its replay system. As a result, one second was placed back on the game clock and an additional play was awarded."

CRAIG CARTON BLASTS MICHIGAN FANS FOR STORMING FIELD AFTER CONTROVERSIAL WIN: 'THEY’RE A BUNCH OF MORONS'

Interestingly, they also stress that the appeal isn't contesting the correct amount of time on the clock, just that the rules were improperly applied.

"This was not a judgment regarding the proper amount of time to place on the clock," it continues. "It was an error in the application of the established replay protocol governing this specific end-of-game timing situation. Had the protocol been properly followed and the program-feed clock been used, no additional play would have been awarded, and Western Michigan would have won the game, 12–7."

MICHIGAN FANS CALLED OUT ON SOCIAL MEDIA FOR RUSHING FIELD AFTER WOLVERINES STEAL WIN OVER WESTERN MICHIGAN

The conference, as a result, want the NCAA FBS Oversight Committee and College Football to recognize the Western Michigan Broncos as the "actual winner."

"The MAC is requesting that those bodies recognize Western Michigan as the actual winner of the game for purposes of their respective rankings, evaluations and selection deliberations, and take such other corrective action as may be within their authority," the statement concludes.

So what does the NCAA rule book actually say about this procedure, and does the MAC have a point? The closest relevant rule seems to govern what video evidence can be evaluated as part of a review. And while it's not overwhelmingly clear what the proper procedure should be, there is an indication that the "televised production" should be used when evaluating video evidence.

"All reviews shall be based upon video evidence provided by and coming directly from the televised production of the game or from other video means available to the replay official that is also available to the television producer," the rule says.

So what chance does the MAC have at getting the result overturned? Very little. Even if there is some truth to this appeal, and the result was unfair to Western Michigan, it's a near impossibility that an FBS Committee overturns a result that was determined on the field. And it goes without saying that big programs like Michigan are a near-certainty to get the benefit of the doubt in these types of cases.

But the MAC at least showed some backbone and support for its member school after that debacle and what it cost them. Western Michigan may have contended for a College Football Playoff spot, with the benefit of a win over a top-20 opponent, had the game ended at 0:00.

In response, the Big Ten issued a statement of their own, saying, "The Big Ten stands by the statement released following the conclusion of the Western Michigan at Michigan game and the determination by the replay officials. We will have no further comment on the matter."

Sums up where both sides are, and why this controversy will never reach a satisfactory resolution for all involved parties.

item.title: American Bishop Robert Barron calls out St. Paul's Cathedral in UK over nightclub partnership
item.description: Roman Catholic Bishop Robert Barron blasted St. Paul's Cathedral for its multi-year Fabric nightclub concert deal, calling it a surrender to secularism.
item.content:encoded:
Bishop Robert Barron criticized London’s historic St. Paul’s Cathedral on Monday over its new partnership with a nightclub company, arguing the venue's upcoming concert series undermines its status as a sacred space.

The Christian Post reported that the Church of England is facing widespread backlash after St. Paul’s Cathedral in London signed a multiyear agreement to host concerts inside the building with Fabric, a nightclub company that lost its license approximately 10 years ago after two drug-related deaths. While the cathedral has worked with the nightclub company before, this latest agreement has sparked an international firestorm of controversy.

Though St. Paul’s belongs to the Anglican Church rather than the Roman Catholic Church, Barron — a prominent American Catholic bishop — wrote a lengthy social media post arguing against misusing the cathedral.

"Word has just come down that St. Paul’s Cathedral in London — the second most important church in the Anglican world — has imitated Canterbury Cathedral in permitting ‘raves,’ nightclub-like entertainments, to take place in its confines," he began.

TOURIST'S CHURCH CLOTHING HACK LEAVES TRAVELERS SHARPLY DIVIDED OVER SACRED-SITE ETIQUETTE

He blasted those who have already emerged to defend the move, saying "The usual reasons for acquiescing to this have been trotted out: reaching out to the young, trying to get with the times, etc. But this development simply shows that the leadership of the Church of England has lost any sense of the crucial distinction between the sacred and the secular."

Barron argued that the whole point of a sacred space is that it is specifically set apart from the mundane, secular world and is meant to "reorient us toward the divine."

"Accordingly, in the properly sacred space, one is lifted out of the conventional and introduced into the numinous. This is why Christian cathedrals are filled with images of the saints and angels and why their interiors are meant first to disorient us and then to reorient us toward the divine," he wrote.

"The contemporary West is, quite literally, the first culture in human history that is in danger of collapsing the sacred into the secular, or better, losing any sense of the difference between the two," he added further. "This is doing enormous damage, especially to young people, whose lives have been flattened into a preoccupation with money, worldly success, and material things. The Church indeed should go out into the secular space to find those who have wandered away from God, but it should then lead those wanderers back to the holy."

EXCLUSIVE VIDEO: BISHOP BARRON TO ADDRESS 'TRUE THREAT TO DEMOCRACY' AT TRUMP PRAYER EVENT

He concluded, "Having ‘raves’ in the nave of one of the most sacred spaces in the Christian world is, I’m sad to say, another sign of our pitiful surrender to ideological secularism."

According to the BBC, the events held at the event venue will be concerts rather than raves.

"Under the partnership, Fabric will be the cathedral's exclusive partner for such events until 2030. The first concert is due to take place on 29 October, although the artist has not been announced," the BBC reported. "Fabric co-founder Cameron Leslie called the deal ‘an extraordinary and unexpected coming together of two very different parts of London.’"

The BBC quoted Sandra Lynes Timbrell, the cathedral's director of visitor engagement, who expressed hope that a "carefully curated programme of exceptional concerts" would draw people who otherwise had not visited the cathedral.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

The controversy mirrors a 2024 dispute at Canterbury Cathedral, which hosted sold-out 90s "silent discos" that critics mocked as a "rave in the nave."

More recently, Canterbury cathedral featured the "Hear Us" art installation, using large stickers simulating graffiti, reportedly inspired by working with "marginalised communities and a team of skilled artists to create vibrant handwritten literature responding to the question: ‘What would you ask God?’" The project was conceived by poet Alex Vellis and curator Jacquiline Creswell.

Fox News Digital reached out to Bishop Robert Barron and Saint Paul's Cathedral and did not receive an immediate reply.

While cathedral leaders argue secular events help attract younger generations, some young believers say church leaders are misjudging what youth actually want.

Catholic actor David Henrie recently told Fox News Digital that he sees young people turning away from secular trends and seeking out traditional faith. Henrie noted an uptick in youth attending traditional Latin Mass services in the United States specifically because they are searching for a clear contrast to modern culture.

"I've seen it coming. I was one of those people who was not living a Christian life and then suddenly found the world was completely empty and was searching for something other worldly," Henrie said. "That's why I think you're seeing kids flock to the faith right now. It's because they're tired of the world."

"[T]hey want 'Lord of the Rings Catholicism,'" Henrie said. "You know, they want bells, smells, ancient expressions of the liturgy. That's where the young people are flocking right now. That's why you're seeing the Latin Mass booming."

Catholic leaders across the U.S. have reported sharp increases in the number of adult converts. A recent Gallup poll also found that 42% of young men now say religion is "very important" in their lives, a 14-percentage-point jump from the previous year.

Fox News' Kristine Parks contributed to this report.

item.title: Legendary sports agent warns MLB lockout would be 'remarkably self-destructive' with CBA set to expire
item.description: Major League Baseball faces its "murkiest" environment since 1994, legendary sports agent Leigh Steinberg told OutKick in a recent interview.
item.content:encoded:
Major League Baseball is just a few weeks away from the postseason as the regular season winds down, but the sport has a different feel this year than in previous years.

Why? The threat of a lockout. The collective bargaining agreement between MLB and the MLBPA expires in December, and the owners are all but guaranteed to lock the players out. Legendary sports agent Leigh Steinberg said this is the "murkiest" environment the sport has had since before the turn of the century.

"This is the murkiest environment that baseball's had since they had the strike back in 1994. Owners seem determined to put in place a salary cap," Steinberg told OutKick in a recent interview.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Steinberg pointed to two major signings by the two-time defending World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers as the straws that broke the camel’s back and outraged owners to the point of wanting a salary cap.

"If you think about it, the contract that signaled all the outrage and incentivized owners to fight for a salary cap was the signing of Kyle Tucker and the thought that who's not playing that well this year, but it was the signing of Kyle Tucker and Edwin Díaz said to people, well, they're doing what the Rams just did," Steinberg said.

As Steinberg said, Tucker has struggled mightily in his first season after signing a four-year, $260 million contract. In 136 games this season, Tucker is hitting just .221 with 12 home runs and 59 RBI with an OPS of just .672.

Those numbers are well below the four-time All-Star’s career batting average of .265 and career OPS of .836.

The Dodgers signed Díaz to a three-year, $69 million contract to become the team’s closer, but the former New York Mets star has been hampered by injuries and has disappointed when on the mound.

LEGENDARY SPORTS AGENT TALKS ABOUT THE RAMS USE OF 'CAPONOMICS' TO BRING AARON DONALD OUT OF RETIREMENT

Díaz, who has been limited to just 16 games because of elbow and neck injuries, has a startling 11.85 ERA in 13 2/3 innings pitched with seven saves. Like Tucker, those numbers are out of the ordinary for him, as he has a career ERA of 3.06 across his 10 seasons in the major leagues.

Yet despite those signings not panning out, the owners are hell-bent on a salary cap, while the players are vehemently opposed. Steinberg warns of dire consequences if the two sides can’t come to an agreement soon.

"[A lockout] would be so self-destructive for baseball. The last time they did that was in 1994. The next year, the gross receipts went down 40%. Fans were angry. They didn't want to come to the games. And it took the steroid-fueled home run race between Mark McGwire and Sammy Sosa and then later Barry Bonds to bring the sport back," Steinberg said.

"It would be remarkably self-destructive."

Steinberg pointed out that revenue has been strong for owners as baseball has seen a resurgence.

"What happens is you need to be able to put yourself in the heart and mind of the other side to negotiate a contract. So, are owners claiming economic turmoil and difficulty?" Steinberg said.

"And the answer is no, because the TV money and attendance and merchandising and fantasy and gambling now. The revenue streams are huge and baseball's had a resurgence."

The famed agent warned of the dire consequences the sport could suffer if both sides lose sight of what is at stake.

"When you get powerful billionaires owning teams locked in with wealthy players, you know, millionaires against billionaires, if you don't have someone able to see the larger picture, you can get deadlocked," Steinberg said.

Both sides have made proposals, but it doesn’t appear that any serious progress has been made in the preliminary talks. In March 2022, the two sides ended a 99-day lockout when MLB and the MLBPA ratified the new collective bargaining agreement.

With owners seemingly more dug in on a salary cap now than they were in 2022, there is concern that both sides would be willing to sacrifice games to get what they want.

Which, as Steinberg said, would be "incredibly self-destructive."

Steinberg, who was inducted into the California Sports Hall of Fame in 2017, has had many high-profile clients throughout his impressive career. Across football and baseball, Steinberg’s clients include Steve Bartkowski, Steve Young, Troy Aikman, Warren Moon, Bruce Smith, Thurman Thomas, Kordell Stewart, Jeff George, Ben Roethlisberger, Myron Rolle, Matt Leinart, Mark Brunell, Ricky Williams, Howie Long, Eric Karros and Dusty Baker, among others.

item.title: Craig Carton, Michael Rapaport dish on their shared dislike for LeBron James: 'Dead to me'
item.description: Craig Carton and Michael Rapaport revealed their reasons for disliking LeBron James during the premiere of OutKick's "The Craig Carton Show."
item.content:encoded:
Craig Carton and Michael Rapaport have more in common than being die-hard New York Knicks fans: They also share a strong dislike for LeBron James.

Rapaport joined Carton for the premiere of OutKick’s "The Craig Carton Show" releasing on Tuesday, where he called the Philadelphia 76ers star a player he loves to hate. Carton admitted that while he respects James’ game, his No. 1 reason for his dislike stems from an off-the-court incident in 2017.

"I'll tell you the number one reason I'm not a LeBron guy. Number one. There's—it's and it's a clear-cut number one for me, and I think I'm the only guy that views it this way, and it p----es me off, all right. Years ago, when he was in Cleveland, and our country is going through racial issues," Carton said on the premiere of his new show.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"In my opinion, he invented a story that the people spray-painted racial epithets on the gate leading up his driveway."

The Associated Press reported at the time, citing police, that unidentified vandals spray-painted the N-Word on the front gate of James' $20 million home in Brentwood. Police said the incident was reported at around 6:45 a.m. local time and nearly three hours later property management covered it up. No arrests were ever made. 

Carton said that he believed James used the event as a vehicle to include himself in the larger conversation at the time.

"And to me, I'm like, look, there's real racial issues in our country. We acknowledge them. For a guy who's such a prominent African-American to try to get in on the conversation by inventing something that never took place. Dead to me," Carton said. "No one talks about it. It's been forgotten because it never happened. No one has the balls to ask—ask him about it, and I'm like, how do we forget the fact that he intruded himself into this serious conversation about race?"

While Rapaport shares Carton’s disdain for the NBA legend, his reason is much more personal. The actor said he had been cool with James and that they had first met during his rookie year with the Cleveland Cavaliers.

A few years later, Rapaport was with his kids, who were 5 and 7 at the time, and James spurned the kids' request for a picture.

"I don't know what he got up bug up his a-- about Michael Rapaport. I had never said anything bad about him. Never said anything," Rapaport said. "I brought my little kids. They were like five and seven, right? And he like Heismaned."

After that point, Rapaport was turned off by James. Prior to the incident with his kids, Rapaport said he had never said anything bad about the then-Cavaliers star.

"I never said anything bad about him. And I think it was a rumor that a friend of mine might have a girl with a friend, and I was like, that has nothing to do with—these are little kids. And that was when I was like, ‘You’re done,’" Rapaport said.

With James joining the 76ers this offseason, Carton and Rapaport, both passionate Knicks fans, will get to see a lot more of the 41-year-old this season. The 76ers' first game of the season is against the defending champions at Madison Square Garden.

Carton’s show launched Sept. 8 and will feature A-list guests with takes on sports and world events.

item.title: South Park creators mock Trump's Lake Ontario rename and company compliance in mock statement
item.description: Trey Parker and Matt Stone announced "South Park" will be renamed "South America" Tuesday in a jab at Apple Maps and Google Maps over the Lake Ontario name change.
item.content:encoded:
"South Park" co-creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone mocked President Donald Trump's renaming of Lake Ontario to Lake America, as well as Apple Maps and Google Maps acquiescing to the change, in a statement on Tuesday.

"Inspired by the bravery and patriotism of Apple and Google, we are changing the name of South Park to SOUTH AMERICA. We especially want to thank our parent company Paramount -- a Skydance Capitulation," the statement on X read.

The joke announcement followed the series winning an Emmy for Outstanding Animated Program for its 27th season premiere in 2025, which featured Trump in bed with Satan while talking about his alleged Jeffrey Epstein cover-up. 

‘SOUTH PARK’ CREATORS SAY THEY’RE ‘DOWN THE MIDDLE’ DESPITE TRUMP TAKEDOWNS

The episode also mocked Trump's settlement with CBS and its parent company Paramount Global, which signed a $1.5 billion deal to stream the animated series on Paramount+ in 2025.

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House, Apple, Google and Paramount for comment.

Trump signed an executive order last month to rename the lake, which sits on the U.S.-Canada border, amid a breakdown in trade agreements between the U.S. and Canada.

'SOUTH PARK' CREATORS RIP SKYDANCE-PARAMOUNT MERGER AS A 'S---SHOW', BLAME DEAL FOR DELAYING NEW SEASON

"The United States is the greatest protector of the Great Lakes, including the body of water currently known as Lake Ontario," the order stated. "Without the security and investment provided by the United States, this freshwater system would not be open for shipping, recreation, and responsible use to the same extent as it is today."

FOX Business confirmed after the order that both Apple Maps and Google Maps updated their maps to display Lake Ontario as Lake America in response to the order.

CHARLIE KIRK EMBRACES 'SOUTH PARK' PARODY OF HIM IN UPCOMING EPISODE AS A 'BADGE OF HONOR'

Google previously said its Maps service would show "Lake America" to U.S. users after the update, while Canadian users would continue to see "Lake Ontario" and users in other countries would see both names. Apple users from these countries would see similar results.

The companies made similar changes after Trump's executive order to rename the Gulf of Mexico to the "Gulf of America" in 2025.

item.title: SCOTUS rejects Missouri GOP bid to use revised congressional map in midterms
item.description: SCOTUS rejects Missouri Republicans' emergency bid over congressional maps, with Justice Kavanaugh ruling without comment and leaving the GOP-backed map blocked for the midterms.
item.content:encoded:
Justice Brett Kavanaugh on Tuesday denied Missouri's emergency appeal without comment, leaving in place the Missouri Supreme Court's ruling blocking the state's revised Republican-backed congressional map from being used in November's general election. 

Kavanaugh acted alone and did not refer the application to the full Supreme Court.

The decision means Missouri will conduct the general election using its 2022 congressional districts after the state high court ruled the newer map never legally took effect because a voter-backed referendum suspended the law before it could go into effect.

Missouri Attorney General Catherine Hanaway had asked the Supreme Court to intervene after the Missouri Supreme Court ruled last week that the state's revised congressional map could not be used in November, despite having been used during last month's primary election. The emergency appeal was directed to Kavanaugh because he oversees emergency applications arising from the Eighth Circuit.

MISSOURI AG FILES PETITION ASKING SUPREME COURT TO REVIVE TRUMP-BACKED REDISTRICTING MAP

The revised map, backed by President Donald Trump and Missouri Republicans, was designed to make Democratic Rep. Emanuel Cleaver's Kansas City-area district more favorable to Republicans, with the goal of expanding the GOP's congressional delegation from 6-2 to 7-1.

The Missouri Supreme Court ruled the referendum petition filed by opponents after lawmakers approved the new districts prevented the map from taking effect unless voters ultimately approve it. The court concluded the congressional map adopted after the 2020 census "remains in full force and effect for the November 2026 general election."

Hanaway argued the state faced an unprecedented situation after administering its primary election under one set of congressional districts only to be ordered to use another for the general election.

In its emergency filing, Missouri told the Supreme Court it now faced "the unprecedented scenario of being forced to apply a starkly different congressional map in the 2026 General Election." The state argued election officials were uncertain whether they could comply with the Missouri Supreme Court's order with voting scheduled to begin within days.

MISSOURI HIGH COURT BLOCKS GOP-BACKED CONGRESSIONAL MAPS AHEAD OF MIDTERMS; TRUMP BLASTS 'RIDICULOUS' RULING

"Only this Court can prevent Missouri from being forced to disenfranchise hundreds of thousands of voters; and only this Court can ensure that Missouri hosts a timely and lawful federal congressional election," the application said.

Hanaway also called the Missouri Supreme Court's ruling "catastrophic."

"We have just appealed yesterday's catastrophic ruling to the Supreme Court of the United States," she said after filing the emergency appeal. "We look forward to the Court's prompt review of this critical matter, as our ability to hold timely and lawful congressional elections hangs in the balance."

Opponents urged the justices to reject the request, arguing there was no genuine emergency because Missouri officials created the timing problem themselves.

GEORGIA REDISTRICTING BATTLE REVIVED AFTER APPEALS COURT OVERTURNS FEDERAL COURT DECISION

In their response, they argued the state's Secretary of State waited until "the last possible day" to challenge the referendum after implementing the revised map during the congressional primary, hoping the courts would refuse to order a return to the previous districts so close to the general election.

"The Emergency Application for Stay does not present a real emergency," they wrote.

They also argued the Supreme Court should not "reward the Secretary's scheme to outsmart Missouri voters, Missouri law, and the Missouri Supreme Court" by allowing the state to use a map the state's highest court concluded "is not the law and has never been the law."

Kavanaugh's denial leaves the Missouri Supreme Court's ruling in place, meaning Missouri's 2022 congressional map will remain in effect for the November general election.

item.title: Aaron Donald will not travel to Australia for Rams opener against 49ers as team ramp-up process not complete
item.description: Aaron Donald won't travel to Melbourne for the Rams' opener against the San Francisco 49ers, with his season debut now targeting Monday Night Football.
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Rams are running a marathon rather than a sprint with Aaron Donald. That’s why Donald wasn’t included in the team's travel party for Thursday night’s matchup against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia.

Because Donald is not going to play in the opener, Rams coach Sean McVay told reporters on Tuesday.

This is a mild surprise given that McVay said in recent days that all the team's players would travel to Australia.

"He's doing a great job," McVay said of Donald. "I think he'll be ready to go sooner rather than later, but we're making a decision that we think is best for him and for our team.

"He's as great a competitor as there is, wants to be out there, wants to influence and effect positive change for us. But I think he also understands there's a necessary ramp up."

Ultimately, Donald and the Rams decided it was better for the 35-year-old defensive lineman, who came out of retirement on Aug. 30, to continue to prepare for the long haul of the looming season rather than plug him in immediately.

Donald has not played in a game since January 2024.

'WE BACK': AARON DONALD RETURNS TO THE RAMS AND A DEFENSE NOW LOADED WITH MYLES GARRETT AND OTHERS

Donald's next opportunity to play will be on Sept. 21 when the Rams host the New York Giants on Monday Night Football.

That gives Donald an extra 10 days to acclimate and prepare for his season.

And why is that important to the Rams?

They see themselves as not just part of the Super Bowl conversation but at the center of it. They felt that way before Donald rejoined the team and still do heading into Thursday night’s game against the 49ers without him.

That's the reason McVay spent a minute discussing the depth of his defensive line.

The Rams want to simply make sure Donald has every chance to prepare for the long haul of the season by getting more time to prepare for its demands.

The last thing the team wants, a source said, is to put Donald in the lineup just a couple of weeks after returning to team practices and expose him to a soft-tissue injury that could linger throughout the season.

So, again, everyone is looking at this as a marathon to run over 16 games and the postseason rather than sprinting off the line in Week 1.

item.title: DK Metcalf is a big conspiracy theorist: 'I think there is another civilization inside of Earth'

item.content:encoded:
DK Metcalf and his quarterback Aaron Rodgers have a connection on and off the field. The Pittsburgh Steelers teammates have apparently been doing a little bonding over conspiracy theories.

I'm in the same boat as you are at this point. I need to brush up on my conspiracy theories too. I had no idea about this one, which is some sort of version of the Hollow Earth theory.

NASA CHIEF PULLS BACK CURTAIN ON TRUMP UFO FILES AFTER BIZARRE FINDS SURFACE IN BURIED FED RECORDS

Again, all new to me. I'm more into aliens, Bigfoot, and the moon landing. Experts will tell you that the Hollow Earth theory has been debunked, but let's hear DK out and see where he goes with it.

Who knows? He could be on to something.

"Yeah, I'm a big conspiracy theorist. Shout out to my quarterback," he told the outlet with a smile. "I think it's another world. I think there is another civilization inside of Earth."

How does anyone access this other civilization? In Antarctica. That's why you can't book a trip there, according to DK.

HARVARD ASTRONOMER TAPPED TO LEAD WHITE HOUSE UFO COUNCIL SAYS US GOVERNMENT 'BAFFLED BY WHAT THEY ARE SEEING'

AARON RODGERS RECONCILING WITH HIS PARENTS AFTER NEARLY A DOZEN YEARS OF ESTRANGEMENT

It's probably been said before, but I'll go ahead and say it again. Who is breaking a Hollow Earth theory bond? It's not going to be broken by any NFL defense, I can tell you that.

I can also tell you that I'm going to need to hear more about this Hollow Earth theory before I take a side.

item.title: Judge orders Alex Murdaugh murder retrial moved to nearby county
item.description: Alex Murdaugh's double murder retrial moves to Sumter County after a judge ruled Colleton County's jury pool was too compromised for a fair trial.
item.content:encoded:
A South Carolina judge on Tuesday granted a request by Alex Murdaugh that the double-murder retrial for the disgraced attorney be relocated to a new venue.

Judge Debra McCaslin ruled that the trial will take place in Sumter County. Defense lawyers argued that Colleton County's jury pool was tainted by the highly covered original trial.

In her order, McCaslin wrote that Murdaugh can receive a fair trial in Sumter County, adding that it offers adequate security measures, courtroom facilities, and technological capabilities to conduct proceedings.

ALEX MURDAUGH'S 'CHARLESTON OR BUST' PRAYER SHOT DOWN BY PROSECUTORS IN FIGHT OVER 'HOLY CITY' RETRIAL

"The judge considered several factors including the financial impact on Colleton County, the convenience of witnesses, courthouse security, transportation and security of Murdaugh, courtroom facilities, and technological capabilities," the order states.

Murdaugh's attorneys had suggested Charleston or Richland County courthouses for the venue transfer before McCaslin made her ruling.

ALEX MURDAUGH RETURNS TO COURT AS DEFENSE ARGUES FOR RETRIAL MOVE AFTER CLERK SCANDAL POISONED JURY POOL

Fox News Digital has reached out to Murdaugh's attorneys and prosecutors.

Murdaugh was granted a new trial after the South Carolina Supreme Court determined his right to a fair proceeding was violated when it found that former Colleton County Clerk of Court Becky Hill improperly influenced jurors during his 2023 murder trial.

ALEX MURDAUGH WINS NEW TRIAL AFTER COURT CLERK ALLEGEDLY TOLD JURORS NOT TO BE 'FOOLED' BY DEFENSE

As a result, the court unanimously overturned his 2023 convictions and two life sentences.

Murdaugh is charged with murder and weapons offenses for the June 2021 shooting deaths of his wife, Maggie, and 22-year-old son, Paul, at their family estate.

At his 2023 trial, Murdaugh admitted to misleading investigators about his location shortly before his wife and son were shot, but he has consistently denied killing either of them.

Fox News Digital's Wehner contributed to this report.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy juror admitted 'reasonable doubt' but still refused insanity verdict, foreperson says
item.description: Three Lindsay Clancy jurors say a lone holdout admitted having reasonable doubt but still refused to deliver a not guilty by insanity verdict.
item.content:encoded:
Three people who served on the jury in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial are speaking publicly for the first time after last week's mistrial, saying a lone holdout prevented the panel from reaching a unanimous verdict.

The jurors, including the foreperson, said one juror acknowledged having reasonable doubt but still refused to find Clancy not guilty by reason of insanity, according to interviews with NBC10 Boston.

The mistrial came after days of deliberations in the closely watched case against Clancy, the Massachusetts mother accused of killing her three young children in January 2023. 

Clancy admitted to the killings but pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity, arguing she was suffering from severe mental illness at the time. Prosecutors maintained she was criminally responsible for the deaths.

LINDSAY CLANCY JUDGE CALLS MISTRIAL, THEN GRANTS DEFENSE ONE HOUR STAY FOR APPEAL

"He admitted he had reasonable doubt and I started filling out the forms, I was so excited," the foreperson told NBC10 Boston.

But the foreperson said the juror then added, "But I'm still not going to say that she's not guilty by reason of insanity."

The foreperson also told the station she wrote the note to the judge raising concerns that one juror had expressed reasonable doubt but would not agree to a verdict. The three jurors said they became frustrated with the holdout during deliberations, claiming he refused to consider the views of the rest of the panel.

LINDSAY CLANCY ATTORNEY KEVIN REDDINGTON SIGNALS HE'S OPEN TO A DEAL, HOPES DA WILL 'REVISIT' CASE

NBC10 Boston reported it attempted to contact the juror identified by the others as the holdout but had not received a response.

A judge declared a mistrial last week after jurors informed the court they were hopelessly deadlocked following several days of deliberations. 

It remains unclear whether prosecutors will seek to retry the case.

item.title: Mamdani drops massive 9/11 records trove as old claims about Ground Zero come under fire
item.description: Over 170,000 pages released by Mayor Zohran Mamdani reveal internal memos questioning whether Ground Zero air was safe after the 9/11 attacks.
item.content:encoded:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani released more than 170,000 pages of records Tuesday that call into question public claims that the air around Ground Zero was safe to breathe following the 9/11 attacks.

Mamdani's office released an initial trove of approximately 170,000 pages of records, including documents found in 68 boxes at the Department of Environmental Protection in 2025 that date back to the aftermath of the 9/11 attacks.

The records release comes just days before the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks in which 2,977 people were killed. Thousands of people exposed to the toxic dust and debris after 9/11 have since died from illnesses associated with the attacks, while many more continue to suffer from health conditions, according to the World Trade Center Health Program and other health authorities.

AMERICA’S HEARTLAND COMES FACE-TO-FACE WITH 9/11 HISTORY AS 25TH ANNIVERSARY NEARS

Then-EPA Administrator Christine Todd Whitman said in a Sept. 18, 2001, press release that monitoring results indicated the air near the World Trade Center was safe to breathe, following EPA assurances about environmental hazards dating to Sept. 13.

"People got sick because the leaders they trusted lied and told them they were safe to breathe in toxic air," Mamdani shared during a Tuesday press conference.

The documents revealed that ten months after the terrorist attacks, traces of asbestos were found on the roof of a building located at 15 John Street, less than a mile from where the World Trade Center once stood.

The records show that asbestos was detected at some locations at levels below applicable cleanup or exposure benchmarks and at others at levels that appeared to exceed them; health authorities have said there is no known safe level of asbestos exposure.

Among the approximately 170,000 pages released through the online portal is a Feb. 28, 2002, memo from then-Mayor Michael Bloomberg's senior policy adviser, summarizing Rep. Jerrold Nadler's concerns about indoor air quality in Lower Manhattan and warning that the city could face public-relations and legal problems over the cleanup.

The memo laid out Nadler's concerns that the Environmental Protection Agency had "handed over responsibility for measuring indoor air quality to the City" without putting in place oversight measures. The memo said the city had passed responsibility for indoor monitoring to property owners and noted that the Health Department had instructed residents to clean buildings with wet mops and rags.

"If Nadler’s concerns are justified, we are not Informing people of the real health risks In lower Manhattan, the City may face major public relations problems and Is leaving Itself open to a barrage of lawsuits," the memo, dated Feb. 28, 2002, stated. "At the least we should discontinue telling people to clean their apartments with wet mops and rags. We should be asking FEMA for funds to support Indoor cleanup."

AS AMERICAN PRIDE HITS A 25-YEAR LOW, A NEW 9/11 EDUCATION PLATFORM URGES THE NATION TO NEVER FORGET

Among the clearest evidence of lingering asbestos contamination near Ground Zero was a finding at Stuyvesant High School, where testing later revealed elevated asbestos in auditorium carpeting.

The school, located less than half a mile north of the World Trade Center, recorded what concerned parents described as "extremely high levels of asbestos" in its auditorium during testing in August 2002.

Nearly a year after the attacks, testing of a carpet sample from the school's auditorium using an EPA-recognized ultrasonication method found asbestos concentrations measured at roughly 2.5 million structures per square centimeter.

For comparison, the EPA's Lower Manhattan Test and Clean Program later called for professional cleaning when settled dust exceeded 5,000 asbestos structures per square centimeter. The Stuyvesant sample was roughly 500 times higher than that cleanup benchmark.

I LOST MY WIFE ON 9/11. PLEASE LET THIS 25TH ANNIVERSARY BELONG TO THE FAMILIES

The parents' findings also reached city officials. A copy of the press release announcing the asbestos results was transmitted through the NYC Department of Environmental Protection's Bureau of Public Affairs on Aug. 7, 2002.

In July 2002, more than 10 months after the attacks, the Independence Plaza North Tenant Association (IPNTA) wrote to the EPA arguing the agency's cleanup of two Tribeca residential buildings had not gone far enough, while also urging broader environmental testing."

The work on this project has thus far been done in an unprotected, hence possibly dangerous manner, allowing the dust from the old carpet being torn up to seep into tenants’ apartments, under and around their doors," Diane Lapson, the tenant association's environmental chair, wrote in the letter.

Lapson also criticized what she described as the EPA's and New York City's Department of Environmental Protection's reliance on visual inspections to assess conditions at Independence Plaza's buildings, including 310 Greenwich St. and 80 North Moore St., arguing the agencies should instead conduct more comprehensive testing.

She urged officials to use ultrasonication to more reliably measure the amount of asbestos still in the buildings."

Based on the illnesses that have plagued IPN residents since 9/11 (constant respiratory, sinus, bronchial, skin rashes, eye infections, headaches, etc.), we believe there is a need to do a thorough cleaning of the entire complex.

CBC CAVES ON 9/11 'TERRORISM' GUIDANCE AS US, CANADIAN OFFICIALS UNLEASH CROSS-BORDER BACKLASH

By September 2002, about two months after Lapson’s letter, the EPA announced that eight contracts had been awarded for asbestos cleanup throughout the downtown area including the ZIP code encompassing Independence Plaza North.

But EPA litigation records show that asbestos contamination remained in some Lower Manhattan apartments months after the cleanup work began.

Lori Mogol and Richard Zimbler, a couple who lived at Independence Plaza North, still had elevated levels of asbestos in their apartment as late as February 2003.

Specifically, their dining room had more than double the EPA’s risk-based clearance level for asbestos, according to tests performed by their assigned contractor.

item.title: First regular-season AP Top 25 poll features expected shuffling after shaky Week 1 of college football
item.description: The Week 1 AP Top 25 poll saw LSU surge three spots after a 51-10 rout of Clemson in Lane Kiffin's debut, while Michigan dropped out entirely.
item.content:encoded:
The first regular-season AP Top 25 college football poll is here, and you'll never guess what happened.

Some teams fell in the polls, others rose, and a total of five programs remained exactly where they were in the preseason poll. While the Week 1 slate of games around the country didn't necessarily jump off the page, teams were awarded by sending messages (hello, LSU), while others left some voters aggressively scratching their heads (we're looking at you, Michigan).

SEC TEAMS WENT 16-0 IN WEEK 1, IS THE CONFERENCE BACK ON TOP OF COLLEGE FOOTBALL WORLD?

Virginia is the lone team in the poll that was unranked the week prior, but when it comes to the biggest jumpers and fallers, the aforementioned Tigers and Wolverines earned the two respective titles.

LSU embarrassed Clemson 51-10 to begin the Lane Kiffin era in Baton Rouge on Saturday night, moving up three spots from 11th in the preseason poll. As for Michigan, it needed an additional second added to the clock and a Mulligan Hail Mary attempt from quarterback Bryce Underwood to beat Western Michigan 13-12, and as a result, fell out of the poll after entering the week ranked 16th.

Oregon may have passed the stiff test Boise State delivered to the tune of a 34-27 victory, but the unexpected, four-quarter battle with the Broncos led voters to move Oregon down four spots from the preseason No. 2 spot.

Like Oregon, SMU avoided a close call on the road at Florida State on Monday, but moved up two spots to 17th after escaping Tallahassee with a 27-24 win. Washington, however, suffered a similar fate to its Big Ten counterparts in the polls after a sloppy 24-10 win in the Apple Cup over Washington State on Sunday.

In terms of surprises in the Week 1 poll, well ... there aren't any, which is refreshing in this over-reactionary era despite most teams around the country having played just one game.

Michigan still received 69 votes to be ranked after Week 1, while Western Michigan received 12.

item.title: Aaron Judge Back In Yankees Lineup Following 99-Day Rib Injury Absence
item.description: Aaron Judge is returning to the New York Yankees after a 99-day absence caused by a broken rib, starting in right field and batting third against the Colorado Rockies.
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Judge returned to the New York Yankees after a 99-day absence caused by a broken rib, starting in right field and batting third Tuesday night against the Colorado Rockies.

A three-time AL MVP, Judge had missed 84 games since his last appearance on May 31. The 34-year-old skipped a minor league injury rehabilitation assignment.

Judge entered hitting .248 with 17 homers, 38 RBIs and a .907 OPS. He was initially injured attempting to avoid second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. during an unsuccessful try for a diving catch at Houston on April 26 and batted .263 with seven homers and 20 RBIs in 31 games before going on the injured list. 

He had just one homer in 18 games before the IL stint. New York was 36-23 after Judge last played on May 31 and went 45-39 in his absence. 

The Yankees hit .243 with 86 homers and a .770 OPS in 59 games through May 31 but .227 with 107 homers and a .681 OPS while Judge was sidelined. Their batting average during that stretch ranked 29th among the 30 major league teams, ahead of Seattle at .225.

New York entered 81-62, four games behind of AL East-leading Tampa Bay and two games in front of Boston (80-65) for the top AL wild card. The Yankees hold a potential tiebreaker over the Red Sox after winning the season series.

Judge hit a career-high .331 with 53 homers and 114 RBIs in 152 games last year, winning his third MVP and first batting title. He missed 10 games from July 26 to Aug. 4 with a flexor strain in his right elbow that he sustained on a throw to home plate July 22 in Toronto. He underwent a plasma-rich platelet injection and did not require offseason surgery.

Judge skipped a rehab assignment in 2023 when he missed 42 games with a fractured right big toe after crashing into the right-field fence at Dodger Stadium. He hit .245 with 18 homers, 35 RBIs and a .965 OPS over 57 games after his return.

Reporting by the Associated Press.

item.title: Georgia Bulldogs place game one highlights behind paywall as post-NIL college football becomes more soulless
item.description: The Georgia Bulldogs posted a game highlight film behind a $20 paywall on a third-party site called Glory Glory, and fans are furious about it.
item.content:encoded:
I read your comments. I read all of them.

Every time I post an article about college football, I scroll down to the comments section to see what the readers are talking about.

And it doesn't matter if the article is about Dabo Swinney going down with the ship at Clemson or Texas Tech's stiffest competition in the Big 12, the majority of the comments are always the same.

SUBSCRIBE TO 'THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW' ON YOUTUBE

"Who cares? NIL has ruined the sport anyway."

Most of the time, I just roll my eyes and move on with my day.

College football is my favorite sport, and although NIL and unlimited player movement — among other things — has made the sport more of a headache to follow, I will still gleefully park my butt in front of my television on Saturday morning and try to soak up as many games as I can.

This latest development, however, may have me joining the doomsday prophets in the comments section.

The Georgia Bulldogs played a game against an overmatched opponent this past Saturday. It doesn't matter who, because they kicked the crap out of them.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL IS FINALLY BACK AFTER MONTHS OF NCAA LAWSUITS, NIL DRAMA AND CONGRESSIONAL FIGHTS

After the game, the football team's official X account posted a teaser trailer for their week one highlight film, complete with a link to go see the whole thing.

There was just one problem: the video is behind a $20 paywall.

The worst part is that the link doesn't even take fans to the UGA athletic department's website, but rather a third-party site called Glory Glory.

Glory Glory is described as "a fan-first ecosystem designed to capture and share exclusive content, deliver unparalleled access to UGA athletics, and inspire deeper levels of engagement."

In layman's terms (at least how I understand it), you pay money to this site which then goes towards the players' NIL funds, and in turn, the fans get team-related content and access.

Judging by the comments underneath the video, this is a nearly universally reviled practice, and I can't blame them.

Where does it end?

HERE'S WHY, EVEN WITH ALL ITS PROBLEMS, COLLEGE FOOTBALL IS STILL BETTER THAN THE NFL

We have rev share. We have NIL collectives. We even have places like Tennessee implementing "talent fees" on season tickets that go towards, you guessed it, NIL.

This is all in addition to millionaire and billionaire boosters footing large portions of the NIL bill as it stands.

None of this is sustainable, and it's why places like the federal government have become battlegrounds to try and "save college sports."

No one likes this, yet it will continue to happen.

I can't see myself ever losing my love for college football; I'm too indoctrinated at this point.

I am, what many would call, a "sicko."

But a large portion of fans are already becoming disillusioned with the sport, and it's things like Georgia's paywall tactic that are inflicting the bulk of the damage.

The death of college football may happen by way of "death by 1,000 papercuts," and we are already a couple hundred cuts deep.

Time to stop the bleeding before the greatest sport on earth becomes a husk of its former self, if it isn't already too late.

item.title: Burrito-eating record smashed, Elizabeth Holmes doc trailer captivates the nation, fictional dog list debate
item.description: This Happy Post-Labor Tuesday Nightcaps covers Nathan Fielder's Elizabeth Holmes documentary, Leah Shutkever's burrito record, and a dog tier list.
item.content:encoded:
Happy Post-Labor Tuesday edition of Nightcaps to you, a real bittersweet day on the ol' "The Far Side" desk calendar, if ever there was one.

It's the symbolic end of summer, but with that comes football (and more importantly, hockey), and what a weekend it was.

But even though Summer '26 is pretty much over, I've saved one summertime ritual for September: a road trip.

My wife and I (plus another passenger I will get into in a moment) will be driving from Orlando, Florida, to Pennsylvania Dutch Country to celebrate my old man retiring after 35 years of service in law enforcement.

Also, there's an Iron Maiden concert nearby, but that was just a very happy coincidence.

I wouldn't miss it for the world, but that doesn't mean I'm not going to still try to save a few bucks.

The original plan was to fly, and it was two things: inconvenient for when we were going and expensive.

15 DOG ESSENTIALS THAT MAKE LATE-SUMMER WALKS AND ROAD TRIPS EASIER

So, I convinced my wife that it would be better to drive over two days.

But I also convinced her that we could save even more cheddar if we brought our French bulldog, Carl, with us.

Now, the numbers check out. I stand by that. I'm also excited to give our newish Ford Bronco Sport a proper long-distance test. However, I'm starting to sweat it a little because if this road trip doesn't go off without a hitch, I will hear about it for the rest of my life.

And I mean, I won't get a break from "...remember how you made us drive to Pennsylvania?" ending any semi-heated discussion until I settle into a pine box for the ol' dirt nap.

I think it'll be good. I've planned it out to avoid traffic in major cities and also to make sure we're on the road so I can listen to F1 practice on the radio (don't tell my wife that part, though).

Hopefully, it's entirely uneventful, and the biggest issue we encounter is a free continental breakfast somewhere in the wilds of North Carolina with a broken waffle iron.

Anyway, enough about my yapping... actually, that's a lie, but we will move on to yapping about other stuff.

I went to see "Coyote vs. Acme" this weekend (which was great), and that meant sitting through about half an hour of trailers, ads, and Nicole Kidman waxing poetic about the magic of movies.

Half an hour before a movie that was only an hour and forty minutes...

Anyway, none of those trailers hold a candle to the one that dropped on Monday for awkward-moment GOAT Nathan Fielder's documentary about disgraced tech leader Elizabeth Holmes, "You Can See Everything."

BOX OFFICE COMEBACK: HOW SUMMER 2026 OFFERS A GLIMMER OF HOPE FOR HOLLYWOOD IN THE POST-COVID ERA

Even if you don't know what it's about, it might make your skin crawl; if you do, it will absolutely make you squirm.

Holmes famously lied a lot about her company Theranos' capabilities and defrauded people out of millions, which landed her in the clink.

So, her staring at Fielder, talking about how she wouldn't deceive him? Yeah, it feels a little like you're looking at a female Hannibal Lecter with a more socially acceptable diet.

The three-hour documentary got rave reviews in its surprise screening, but more importantly, it birthed a slew of memes.

Well, I think I'll have to clear a couple of hours and check that puppy out when it comes out in October.

And if you've never seen "Nathan For You," you probably have a friend who will talk your ear off about it.

I used to be a big Guinness Book of World Records guy when it was all about fat motorcycle twins and people clipping dozens of clothespins to their face, but it's gotten a little ridiculous. Most of the time it's just people doing things that no one ever really thought to do before, and are therefore records.

Like, I could balance a few books on the end of a plunger and — voila! — record.

So, it made me happy to see an old-school-style record courtesy of Great Britain's Leah Shutkever.

That record? Housing a burrito faster than any human being ever has before... when being filmed on camera by the people from Guinness.

Did anyone else just think of some David Attenborough-narrated nature documentary where a python swallows an antelope whole, or was that just me?

What a display, and nice to see the British loosening up a little on the manners front. Tough to be on the forefront of competitive eating if you're more concerned with which fork goes where instead of cramming tortilla, rice, and beans into your food hole.

SUBSCRIBE TO 'THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW' ON YOUTUBE

Congratulations, Leah. We can't wait to see what you gorge yourself on next.

In my humble opinion, one of the greatest bits of the last 35 years is Triumph the Insult Comic Dog.

The brainchild of comedy great Robert Smigel, I can throw on a Triumph bit from "Late Night" that I've already seen dozens of times and laugh hysterically like it's brand new.

It's genius.

However, Triumph may have taken a wrong step, and it was all because of his tier list of TV and movie dogs.

He's No. 1 — which I can live with — but after that, things get wild.

That's a great list... for me and the rest of the internet to poop on!

Wishbone on the same tier as Scrappy-Doo? One is a Jack Russell Terrier who exposed a generation to literary classics, while the other is Scooby's nephew that everyone hates.

And Air Bud in the "Near Great" tier? Did I imagine this, or is he a multi-sport athlete who has bailed out multiple teams over the years?

Those are my gripes; others had theirs.

There are also a few omissions I think we need to include.

First is Muttley of "Wacky Races" fame, who I think needs to go in the average tier. Not a bad sidekick for Dick Dastardly, but could've been near-great had he helped him pull off more evil schemes successfully.

The other one is Tiger from "The Brady Bunch," who was an abject failure.

Do you realize how bad you have to be to get written out of "The Brady Bunch" when they chose to write in Cousin Oliver?

...

That's it for today's edition of Nightcaps! See you tomorrow!

item.title: Joe Biden shares health update after prostate cancer diagnosis while issuing warning to others
item.description: Joe Biden revealed his radiation treatment from last fall "worked as intended" as he urged men to discuss prostate cancer screening with their doctors.
item.content:encoded:
Former President Joe Biden shared an update on his battle with prostate cancer Tuesday, revealing that radiation treatment he underwent last fall "worked as intended" while urging American men not to delay conversations with their doctors about cancer screening.

Biden, 83, issued the update in a lengthy social media post marking Prostate Cancer Awareness Month, saying the occasion was more personal for him following his diagnosis last year.

"The radiation treatment from last fall worked as intended, and I continue to do the things I care about, like finishing my memoir," Biden wrote.

JILL BIDEN SAYS FORMER PRESIDENT WILL LIVE WITH STAGE 4 CANCER 'FOR THE REST OF HIS LIFE,' HAS SLOWED DOWN

He also thanked the doctors, nurses and other medical professionals who have treated him, saying their "skill, dedication, and compassion mean so much."

Biden used much of the message to urge men to discuss prostate cancer screening with their doctors, pointing to the dramatically higher survival rate when the disease is detected early.

CANCER TREATMENT DELAYS SURGE ACROSS US AS DOCTOR WARNS SYSTEM ‘NEEDS FIXING IMMEDIATELY’

"Talk to your doctors. Ask the hard questions. Do it for yourself, and do it for the people who love you," Biden wrote.

Biden said men at average risk should begin discussing prostate cancer screening with their doctors around age 50, while Black men and those with a family history should begin those conversations earlier.

SIMPLE SITTING CHANGE LINKED TO LOWER RISK OF CANCER DEATH, STUDY FINDS

The American Cancer Society recommends discussing screening at age 50 for average-risk men, age 45 for Black men and certain men with a family history, and age 40 for some men at even higher risk.

Biden’s office announced in May 2025 that the former president had been diagnosed with an aggressive form of prostate cancer that had metastasized to his bones.

JOE BIDEN'S CANCER HAS SPREAD FURTHER, LEAVING HIM IN 'VERY PAINFUL' CONDITION, HUNTER REVEALS

The diagnosis came after Biden experienced increasing urinary symptoms and doctors discovered a prostate nodule. His office said at the time that the cancer had a Gleason score of 9, Grade Group 5, but was hormone-sensitive, allowing for effective management.

Biden later underwent radiation therapy and completed that course of treatment last fall.

CANCER SURVIVORS SAW MAJOR IMPROVEMENTS IN SLEEP AND WELL-BEING WITH ONE WEEKLY PRACTICE

Fox News Digital reached out to Biden’s office for additional comment on his current health, treatment and prognosis.

Biden closed Tuesday's message by thanking those who have continued to pray for him and his family.

"It’s my hope and prayer that by sharing our experience and being part of this important conversation, we can help save lives," he wrote. "And no matter what, keep the faith. God bless you."

Fox News Digital's Stepheny Price and Robert McGreevy contributed to this reporting.

item.title: Fetterman leans on unlikely GOP ally as Dems sharpen their knives over explosive report
item.description: Senate Democrat John Fetterman calls leaked staff texts about skipping constituent meetings "smears" as Dave McCormick defends him on social media.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., is under fire over leaked texts with his staff in which he brushed off meetings with a children’s hospital and paralyzed veterans, but he is pushing back, calling the reports "smears" with support from his Republican Pennsylvania colleague, Sen. Dave McCormick.

Fetterman broke his silence following a bombshell report based on leaked text messages between him and his staff that portrayed him as brushing off basic duties of being a senator, including meetings with constituents.

Fetterman told CNN in a statement that "disgruntled" staffers had concocted the story, first reported by the Wall Street Journal, to knock his reputation.

FETTERMAN FACES DEM REVOLT AS BOMBSHELL REPORT FUELS PUSH TO OUST HIM: 'DISGRACE'

"Per usual — lies, half-truths, innuendos, smears and anonymous," Fetterman said.

"No matter how many smears or stories, I’m proud to continue to deliver for Pennsylvania," he continued.

The lawmaker’s response follows an explosive report published last week that painted Fetterman as a politician more interested in appearing on Fox News to discuss Israel than meeting with constituents, including a group of paralyzed veterans from his state, and opting to blow off a funeral for slain police officers because it would have taken too long.

While other Democratic members of the Pennsylvania delegation were furious with Fetterman, his fellow senator, McCormick, came to his defense.

"These stories are the latest example of outrageously disloyal staff and forces on the Left using anonymous leaks to cancel my friend John Fetterman," McCormick said on X. "They hate that he is an independent thinker who refuses to fall into line so they want to silence him."

WHY TRUMP, GOP ARE COURTING JOHN FETTERMAN, WHO INSISTS HE’LL REMAIN A DEMOCRAT

Fetterman and McCormick share a unique relationship in a Congress that has grown increasingly partisan. They’re one of three Senate duos from a purple state, and Fetterman has vowed to not support an opponent when and if McCormick runs for re-election in 2030.

"Well, I would absolutely never move against my friend," Fetterman told reporters.

They also launched a joint fundraising effort in July, called Common Ground PA, according to federal financial filings.

DNC VICE CHAIR ATTACKS DEMOCRATIC SEN. JOHN FETTERMAN: 'YOU’RE A MESS'

And the pair spent Labor Day together, per a post from McCormick, where they toured Bell & Evans, a chicken processing company in Pennsylvania.

"He and I will continue to work together to deliver for Pennsylvania by saving jobs at US Steel, passing a new law to make housing more affordable, securing $600 million to replace the Delaware River Bridge, and delivering critical funding to protect Presque Isle State Park," McCormick continued.

Still, members of the Pennsylvania delegation and beyond, including the vice chair of the Democratic National Committee, are laying the groundwork to oust him.

Rep. Chris Deluzio, D-Pa., a progressive representing southwest Pennsylvania, charged that Fetterman’s behavior was "pathetic," and said that "this man has no sense of duty."

Whether Fetterman mount a bid for re-election in 2028 remains to be seen.

"He is not up for the high office he was elected to — and we in Pennsylvania will do something about it in 2028," Deluzio said on X.

item.title: AI shopping carts could drive up your grocery bill
item.description: AI-powered smart grocery carts are linked to 32% higher spending, according to new research, as Instacart Caper Carts expand across U.S. stores.
item.content:encoded:
Artificial intelligence is making its way into the grocery aisle, and it could have an unexpected effect on how much you spend. You grab a grocery cart, start working through your list and notice a screen on the handle offering directions, coupons and product suggestions. It can keep a running total and may even let you skip the checkout line. That sounds convenient. It also gives the store a new way to reach you while you are deciding what goes into your cart.

New research found that shoppers who chose a smart shopping cart spent 32% more on average than people using a regular cart. They also bought more items and stayed in the store longer. So the question for you is pretty simple: Does a smarter cart help you shop better, or does it make spending more a little too easy?

Here's how the study worked, where these smart carts are already showing up in the U.S. and how to use one without letting it push your grocery bill higher.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the Protect Your Money replay

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, Protect Your Money From Today’s Biggest Threats, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our financial protection checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five simple ways to help defend yourself against AI scams, fraud, identity theft and financial hacks. You’ll learn how to set up bank alerts, strengthen your account logins, protect your phone number, freeze your credit and help secure your retirement savings against unauthorized transfers. No technical experience is needed.

Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

NEW AMAZON AI SEARCH TURNS WORDS INTO SHOPPABLE IMAGES

The research comes from Bayes Business School at City St George's, University of London. The study, published in the Journal of Business Research, looked at how digital shopping carts were associated with spending and shopping behavior. Researchers studied smart shopping carts at a well-known German supermarket chain during March 2025.

They analyzed 12,418 individual shopping sessions over the month. Of those trips, 9,422 involved shoppers actively using the smart-cart technology. These were grocery carts fitted with tablet-style screens on the handle. Shoppers could use the technology for digital shopping lists, personalized recommendations and in-store navigation. The carts also supported checkout-free payment.

Researchers recorded how much shoppers spent and how many items they bought. They also measured how long each shopping trip lasted. The differences were substantial.

Smart-cart shoppers spent 32% more on average than non-users. They also purchased 25% more items and spent 23% more time in the store. The spending gap grew during afternoons and weekends. Meanwhile, shoppers tended to spend the most time in stores during the evening.

Those numbers naturally caught the researchers' attention because a cart that increases shopper engagement could become a valuable tool for stores. Dr. Sabrina Gottschalk, a lecturer in marketing at Bayes Business School and lead author of the study, said the findings suggest retailers could see significant revenue gains from the technology.

She pointed to special offers and new product recommendations as potential opportunities. The screen also creates another place for retailers and brands to advertise while someone is actively deciding what to buy. That last part catches my attention. The screen may help you find something faster. At the same time, it can put another product in front of you when you are already in shopping mode. Your grocery cart has essentially become another screen competing for your attention.

There is an important limitation here. The study found an association between smart-cart use and higher spending. Because the researchers observed shopping behavior rather than randomly assigning shoppers to different carts, the results do not prove that the technology itself caused the 32% increase.

Someone choosing a smart cart may already have planned a bigger grocery run. A shopper with a longer list could also be more interested in technology designed to make navigating the store easier. Then researchers found another wrinkle.

They looked at shoppers who interacted with the smart-cart screen more than 20 times during a single trip. These "superusers" bought significantly more items and stayed in the store longer. However, they did not spend more money overall. Once screen interaction reached higher levels, spending and basket size eventually began to decline.

Researchers suggested that some of these shoppers may have been using the technology more for the experience than because they wanted to buy more. So the research does not prove that tapping a smart-cart screen automatically sends your grocery bill soaring. Still, a 32% difference in average spending is hard to ignore.

BABY BOOMERS HATE 10 THINGS ABOUT TODAY'S GROCERY STORES

While this particular study happened in Germany, smart carts are already rolling through grocery stores here in the U.S. Instacart says thousands of its AI-powered Caper Carts are deployed across more than 100 cities. The company also said in May 2026 that Caper Carts spanned 15 states and were available across more than a dozen retail banners overall. U.S. retailers using the technology include Kroger and Schnucks, along with Wakefern banners such as ShopRite and Fairway Market. Weis Markets has also begun deploying them at select stores.

Caper Carts use cameras, built-in scales and other sensors to understand what shoppers put into or remove from their baskets. The screen can also deliver recommendations while customers move through the store. Amazon has a competing version called Dash Cart.

Its newest Dash Cart displays prices and keeps a running total as you shop. It can offer personalized nearby deals, help navigate the store and let shoppers bypass the traditional checkout line. Amazon says the newest version will expand to dozens of additional Whole Foods Market locations across the U.S. by the end of 2026. That means this technology could become a much more familiar part of your grocery run.

Here is where I think smart carts become especially interesting. A traditional shopping cart holds your groceries. A smart cart can also put promotions directly in front of you while you move around the store.

Instacart says its Caper Cart technology can use signals such as what is already in your basket and where the cart is inside the store to decide when to surface recommendations. The company says prompts designed to remind shoppers about forgotten items have increased average basket size in its own testing. Think about how powerful that can be.

You turn down an aisle and a promotion appears for something nearby. Something already in your cart could also lead to a recommendation for another product. Sometimes that could save you money or remind you about something you genuinely need. Other times, you may end up buying something that never appeared on your shopping list. Retailers have spent decades figuring out where to position products. Smart carts bring another version of that strategy directly onto a screen that moves through the store with you.

There is also a data side to these carts that deserves attention. Instacart says its Caper Carts use basket-facing camera sensors and outward-facing cameras. They also rely on built-in scales and location-tracking systems.

The company says those systems can detect which products enter or leave the basket and how shoppers move through store aisles. Instacart also says its technology can connect physical shopping interactions with purchase history. That data can make the cart more useful. It can also help make recommendations more targeted.

That is why I would pay attention to the privacy settings connected to any grocery-store account or loyalty program you use. Take a look at what information the retailer collects and what controls it gives you over personalized advertising.

MARYLAND MOVES TO BAN SURVEILLANCE PRICING IN GROCERY STORES

You do not have to avoid an AI shopping cart simply because there is a screen attached to it. Some of the technology can genuinely make grocery shopping easier. The key is using those features without letting every recommendation change what you planned to buy.

Decide what you need before you enter the store. When the cart suggests something extra, compare it with the list you already made.

This could actually be one of the best features of a smart cart. Keep an eye on your total as you shop instead of waiting for the final surprise at checkout.

A recommendation may be useful, but remember why it appeared on your screen. The retailer benefits when another product lands in your cart.

Do not assume a coupon or promoted product gives you the best deal. Compare prices and look at the unit price when package sizes differ.

Here is a simple experiment you can do yourself. Compare what you spend during a few smart-cart trips with your regular grocery runs. You may discover the technology helps you stay organized. You could also find that those convenient suggestions are adding more to your bill than you realized. For more ways to cut grocery costs, check out our article on 8 apps that can cut your food bill.

I like technology that removes some of the aggravation from grocery shopping. Seeing your running total can be useful. Getting out of the store without standing in a long checkout line sounds pretty appealing to me too. What I want you to remember is that the screen on your cart has another purpose. Retailers can use it to put offers and recommendations in front of you at exactly the moment you are deciding what to buy. That does not make every suggestion a bad deal. Some could genuinely save you money. Still, the 32% spending difference in this study caught my attention. As these carts become more common in grocery stores, I think we should pay as much attention to how they influence our shopping as we do to how much time they save us. Enjoy the convenience and take the discounts when they really help. Most of all, keep your shopping list and your budget in charge.

Would you grab an AI-powered shopping cart if it helped you skip the checkout line, or would knowing smart-cart users spent 32% more make you stick with a regular cart? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.
